sentences.text: Magnapaulia was a herbivorous dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in Baja California, northwestern Mexico, and it is the only known species of this extinct lambeosaurine ornithopod dinosaur.
The original describer estimated the animal reached lengths of 15 to 16.5 meters and weighed up to 8 metric tons, while another estimate suggested a weight of over 23 tons.

A 2012 study estimated the length at around 12.5 meters, identifying it as the largest known lambeosaurine based on a specimen with an 80.3 cm humerus, and suggested the animal could have weighed up to 9.77 metric tons.

Unique features include tail chevrons four times longer than vertebrae and front joint processes at the tail base forming a deep trough, alongside a tall crest of spines running from the middle of the back to the middle of the tail with spines four times higher than the vertebrae.
Skin impressions show large scales up to four centimeters wide surrounded by smaller hexagonal and rounded scales.

The species was first described in 1981 by William J. Morris as Lambeosaurus laticaudus based on a partial skeleton and skull, originally named ?L. laticaudus because a complete crest had not been found at the time.
The specific name laticaudus means "broad tail" in Latin, and the generic name combines the Latin word for "large" with the first name of Paul G. Haaga, Jr.
The genus was elevated to a separate genus in 2012 by Prieto-Márquez, Chiappe, and Joshi, after Alberto Prieto-Márquez and colleagues assigned the animal to its own genus.
Magnapaulia fossils were found in Upper Cretaceous rocks in Baja California, northwestern Mexico.

Morris considered the species semiaquatic, interpreting its large size and high, narrow tail as adaptations for swimming, and thought a healed broken femur was evidence that a terrestrial animal would not have survived long enough to heal such an injury.
Magnapaulia is classified within the subfamily Lambeosaurinae, and the genus was assigned to the subfamily Lambeosaurinae in 2012.
The parent group of Magnapaulia is Lambeosaurini, it belongs to the family Hadrosauridae, and Magnapaulia is classified in the class Ornithischia.

Cladistic analysis places Magnapaulia closest to Velafrons, forming a southern clade sister to northern Asian and North American lambeosaurines, and a 2012 cladistic analysis placed Magnapaulia close to Velafrons, identifying it as the sister species.
Between 1981 and 2012, researchers debated whether the remains belonged to Lambeosaurus, Hypacrosaurus, or represented a valid new genus.
